extracted.intended_audience: general public interested in foreign affairs, shipping, and government wartime measures
extracted.subtask_short: news reporting on combat zone proclamation
extracted.subtask_description: Newspaper/Associated Press report (April 1940) summarizing President Roosevelt's proclamation extending the European combat zone, related executive orders freezing Norwegian and Danish assets, shipping/evacuation guidance, and diplomatic/military reactions to the German invasion of Norway and Denmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential authority to define combat areas (Neutrality Act / Joint Resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the President shall have issued a proclamation under the authority of Section 1(a), and he shall thereafter find that the protection of citizens of the United States so requires, he shall, by proclamation, define combat areas, and thereafter it shall be unlawful, except under such rules and regulations as may be prescribed, for any citizen of the United States or any American vessel to proceed into or through any such combat area. The combat areas so defined may be made to apply to surface vessels or aircraft, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text notes the President's authority derives from Section 3 of the joint resolution approved Nov. 4, 1939; he may modify or revoke proclamations when conditions cease. The proclamation delegates enforcement diligence to officers charged with the laws and delegates unspecified authorities to the Secretary of State to exercise powers and promulgate rules not inconsistent with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and geographic definition of the European combat zone
rubrics_metrics.description: The proclamation extends the European combat zone from Bergen on the west coast of Norway entirely around the Scandinavian peninsula to the Russian mainland just south of 44 degrees east longitude and 70 degrees north latitude, and then along specified rhumb lines and coastlines returning to the point of beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed coordinates and rhumb-line descriptions are provided in the proclamation (sequence of latitudes/longitudes and coastal boundaries including the Kola peninsula, Archangel, Murmansk, the Baltic Sea and coasts of Germany, Denmark, Netherlands, Belgium, France and Spain). The extension prevents U.S. vessels from operating in those waters and closes some Russian ports to U.S. shipping; exceptions may apply for voyages necessary to bring American citizens out of danger areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlawfulness and penalties for violation by American vessels, owners or officers
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of the violation of any of the provisions of this section by any American vessel, or any owner or officer thereof, such vessel, owner, or officer shall be fined not more than $50,000 or imprisoned for not more than five years, or both. Should the owner be a corporation, officers or directors participating in the violation shall be liable to the penalty hereinabove prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passengers traveling in violation may be fined not more than $10,000 or imprisoned for not more than two years, or both. The proclamation enjoins utmost diligence in preventing violations and bringing offenders to trial and punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for voyages to remove American citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: The proclamation does not make unlawful voyages which are necessary to bring American citizens out of danger areas; such voyages may be permitted under rules and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Department has worked out plans for removing nationals from Norway and Denmark; the proclamation and reporting emphasize that exceptions exist when voyages are needed to evacuate U.S. citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order amendment (EO No. 6560) — freezing Norwegian and Danish property
rubrics_metrics.description: By virtue of authority vested, the President amends Executive Order No. 6560 by adding sections prohibiting dealings in property in which Norway or Denmark or any national thereof is or was the owner, or in which Norway or Denmark or any national thereof has or had an interest of any nature whatsoever, direct or indirect, and with respect to any acquisition, transfer, disposition, or any other dealing in such property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment applies to property and interests on or since April 8, 1940, and empowers the Secretary of the Treasury to prescribe regulations, require reports under oath, and demand production of books, contracts, letters or other papers concerning required reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited financial and monetary transactions involving Norway/Denmark (Section 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding previous provisions, all of the following are prohibited except as specifically authorized in regulations or licenses issued by the Treasury: (A) all transfers of credit between any banking institution within the United States and any banking institution outside the United States; (B) all payments by any banking institution within the United States; (C) all transactions in foreign exchange by any person within the United States; (D) the export or withdrawal from the United States, or the earmarking of gold or silver coin, or bullion or currency by any person within the United States; and (E) any transaction for the purpose or which has the effect of evading or avoiding the foregoing prohibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'banking institution' is broadly defined to include persons engaged in banking, granting or transferring credits, purchasing/selling foreign exchange or procuring purchasers/sellers, including principals, agents, home offices, branches or correspondents regarded as separate banking institutions. Licenses/regulations may authorize exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and information requirements (Section 10 and Treasury authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports under oath shall be filed on such forms, at such times and by such persons as provided in regulations prescribed by the Treasury. The Secretary of the Treasury may require furnishing under oath of additional and supplemental information, including production of books of account, contracts, letters or other papers with respect to matters concerning which reports are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury is authorized to prescribe regulations to carry out Sections 9 to 11 and to provide conditions under which licenses may be granted; the Treasury may designate persons to whom reporting/regulatory conditions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'Norway', 'Denmark', 'national' and scope of covered persons (Section 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms 'Norway' and 'Denmark' mean the State and Government of those countries on April 8, 1940, and include political subdivisions, agencies, dependencies and possessions, and persons acting or purporting to act directly or indirectly for their benefit. A 'national' includes individuals domiciled in, subject, citizens or residents of Norway or Denmark at any time on or since April 8, 1940, and includes partnerships, associations, corporations organized under their laws or which since that date have been controlled by or had substantial stock owned or controlled by such nationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions extend the scope of prohibitions to entities and persons with connections to Norway/Denmark on or after April 8, 1940, but exclude specified persons residing in the United States on April 8, 1940, as noted in the order's language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of presidential powers to Secretaries and agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The President delegates to the Secretary of State the power to exercise any authority conferred on him by the joint resolution and to promulgate rules and regulations not inconsistent with law; the Secretary of the Treasury similarly is authorized and empowered to prescribe regulations to carry out Sections 9 to 11 and to designate conditions under which licenses may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation includes authority to issue regulations, require reports, and administer embargo/freeze measures; other powers may be delegated by executive order to other officers or agencies as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on transactions intended to evade controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Any transaction for the purpose or which has the effect of evading or avoiding prohibitions on transfers of credit, payments, foreign exchange transactions, export/withdrawal/earmarking of specie or currency, is itself prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This catch-all prohibition is emphasized to prevent circumvention via indirect channels; Treasury regulations and licensing authority manage possible exceptions or enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and treatment of banking institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'banking institution' includes any person engaged primarily or incidentally in the business of banking, of granting or transferring credits, of purchasing or selling foreign exchange or procuring purchasers and sellers; each principal, agent, home office, branch or correspondent of any person so engaged shall be regarded as a separate 'banking institution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expansive definition makes interbank transfers and correspondent relationships subject to the prohibitions and reporting requirements; it clarifies applicability to domestic and foreign branches/correspondents of U.S. banks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routes and logistical guidance for removing Americans from Norway/Denmark
rubrics_metrics.description: State Department laid out tentative routes for Americans wishing to leave: (1) by freighter to England from Bergen and Trondhjem, thence to America; (2) south from Oslo to Germany with Nazi permission, then to Italy and out from Genoa; (3) out direct on three American freighters in port at Bergen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans based on standing instructions and availability of ships; State Department has funds to assist destitute Americans and is prepared to send money on promissory notes; communications difficulties and changing on-the-ground conditions may affect options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and conditions for foreign sale of U.S. military aircraft models
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers were told they were free to negotiate foreign contracts for the Lockheed P-38, Bell P-39 and Curtiss P-40D; official authority to sell came after negotiations and included acceptance by the Air Corps of later deliveries with improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangement protects the Army's investment and assures most advanced models for the expanding Air Corps; deliveries likely delayed and substantial production may not occur for possibly a year.
